title: Walkie Talkie teaser
notes: speaker n = narrator (white subtitle), u = what Walkie hears (yellow subtitle, 🎙️ in front). 'target' = seconds of the scene in the cut. Only the local model is shown; never ElevenLabs or Wispr Flow.

scenes.shows: The untouched site with a small opaque Terminal (the coding agent) in the lower-right. He binds it (the bind gesture: the flight to the window, the chip naming the session), then clicks the page: the browser covers the terminal and the chip keeps showing the bound session.

lines.text: Your agent lives in your terminal, but you shouldn't!
Bind it once. Then keep your eyes on what matters,

scenes.shows: Prompt to the bound terminal (right edge dust). The page restyles; Claude's wait is cut.

lines.text: Make the header dark and this button orange.
and just speak your prompt.

scenes.shows: Wheel-drag a box round an element, shift-drag it to a new place (the arrow from the red box to the green one); the element lands exactly there on the page. A high-impact scene: show the precision.

lines.text: Move this up here.
Move elements exactly where you want them.

scenes.shows: While talking: a screenshot, a crop, highlighted text, an image copied from Google Images. The prompt panel shows them inside the sentence where they were made.

lines.text: Use this picture
here, and fix this text.
Everything you point at is inserted in the prompt, at the moment you said it.

scenes.shows: Screen recording mode (REC corners) over a flickering menu.

lines.text: Or film it.
See how this flickers? Fix it.

scenes.shows: A Java class in an IDE-like diff; a for loop summing prices is selected; it is rewritten as items.stream().filter(...).mapToDouble(i -> i.price() * i.qty()).sum() — no reduce.

lines.text: I don't like this loop. Use Streams.

scenes.shows: Five beats: (e) a prompt to the bound session behind the browser, right edge dust; (a) swipe up = new session: the folder dialog open with 3-4 saved folders besides workspace, top edge; (b) the wake word row; (c) a prompt at the caret, bottom edge with red pins; (d) clean dictation with the puzzle (Mosaic) effect and the red caret pin, Transcribing → Redacting → the text landing with Resilience4j spelled right.

lines.text: Send your prompt to the session in the back,
to a new session,
or call out the wake word:
Hey Claude.
or drop it at the cursor.
Or simply dictate: cleaned using a dictionary that keeps learning from your agent sessions.

scenes.shows: Quick question over the real GitHub page of Netflix/Hystrix: left edge question marks, the reply pop-up (No: maintenance mode since 2018, last release 1.5.18, Netflix recommends resilience4j) with web check and adversarial review.

lines.text: Is the Hystrix library from Netflix still maintained?
Question mode: web research, adversarially reviewed.

scenes.shows: Generated card: the checklist of the features shown, all ticked; the last two (All local, Token-efficient) get ticked as their lines are spoken.

lines.text: Everything stays on your machine: your voice, your media.
Token-efficiency tuned with heavy evals.

checklist: Talk to the session in the back
New session · wake word · at the cursor

scenes.shows: End card: Walkie Talkie logo, 'Free · open source · macOS', github.com/victorrentea/walkie-talkie.

lines.text: Walkie Talkie. Talk to your coding agent.
